name: TCB
why: Jeans, work shirts and jackets sewn in the brand's own Kojima, Okayama factory, with named vintage machines and documented process.
origin: Founded in 2007 per press (Heddels 28 Apr 2026); Rope Dye 13 Sep 2017 says 2008; brand's own About gives only 'aged 27' and 2012 first original product in Kojima, Kurashiki, Okayama, Japan (current factory since 2011; where the first home workshop stood is not stated by the brand) by Hajime Inoue (井上一), named founder on the brand's own About and Crews pages.

craft_evidence.owned: Yes (brand's own claim): TCB runs its own sewing factory in Kojima, 1F sewing/2F shop/3F cutting; 'factory brand' that makes and sells its own; machines listed by model incl. six Union Special 35800G. Evidence is the brand's own pages; no filing or photograph checked
craft_evidence.makers: No: product pages say 'designed and made in Japan only by TCB crews' or 'Made in Kojima'; staff first names on /crews; no outside factory named (Reebok x TCB denim is woven in Ibara City, Okayama, mill unnamed)
craft_evidence.mills: Partial: no current mill named on product pages. Cotton origins named instead (Zimbabwe, San Joaquin, Memphis, Texas/Mississippi combed). Brand's About names Cone Mills fabric for the 2012 first product only. Press (Heddels, 28 Apr 2026) names Shinya Mills as weaver of TCB selvedge: press, not brand
craft_evidence.madein: About 7 of about 33 men's product descriptions read state Japan or Kojima (50's Jeans, 50's Slim Jeans T, 60's Jeans, 20's Jeans, Seamens Trousers, Seamens Jacket, 60's Trucker Jacket); the rest are silent. Roughly 20 percent
craft_evidence.heritage: Dated and placed: founder moved to Kojima aged 20, started TCB sewing business aged 27 (no calendar year given by brand), moved to current factory 2011, first original product 2012 for Kojima denim festival, factory renovated 2018 (tcbjeans.com/about)
craft_evidence.process: Yes: /sewing names Union Special 35800G lapped-seam (six machines, 1/4, 9/32, 5/16 inch seam widths), 51800G waistband, 43200G hem, REECE 104 hole-later buttonholes, and why vintage machines suit cotton thread
craft_evidence.reasoning: Owned working factory with documented process (named vintage machines, seam widths, floors) and dated history in Kojima, so the maker and brand are close to one thing. Held at 4, not 5: mills are not named on current product pages, made-in is stated on about a fifth of descriptions, and caps, collab tee and Reebok shoe are made elsewhere or by partners. A 5 is arguable if Sebastian reads factory brand as maker equals brand

ownership.owner: Hajime Inoue named as founder and owner on the brand's English About us page; no filing checked
